proposal: The Mandate recommends that OPM move forward with rigorous, validated skills-based entry assessments (citing USA Hire) in place of self-rated questionnaires, and that disparate-impact doctrine be narrowed by statute or regulation. It also says reforming the Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures could let courts revisit the Carter-era consent decree that ended the PACE exam.

status_summary: EO 14170 (2025-01-20) directed a federal hiring plan with technical and alternative assessments and an 80-day time-to-hire target, and OPM's Merit Hiring Plan (2025-05-29) followed, including USA Hire assessments for 135 job series. OPM ended the long-used ACWA assessment (guidance dated 2026-02-25 per OPM's news listing). EO 14281 (2025-04-23) told agencies to deprioritize disparate-impact enforcement and review consent judgments. Following a 2026-06-09 DOJ Office of Legal Counsel opinion, OPM issued an interim final rule on 2026-07-31 removing references to the Uniform Guidelines from its regulations. The status of the PACE-era consent decree and of the Guidelines at other agencies was not verified.

timeline.event: EO 14170 directs a Federal Hiring Plan: technical and alternative assessments, time-to-hire under 80 days, and senior-leader involvement in hiring.

EO 14281 sets a policy of ending disparate-impact liability to the extent possible, directs agencies to deprioritize its enforcement, and orders review of existing consent judgments and injunctions that rely on it.

OPM and the Domestic Policy Council issue the Merit Hiring Plan: USA Hire validated assessments for 135 job series, subject-matter-expert assessment strategies, and short essay questions (guidance 2025-06-23, updated 2026-04-30).
OPM announces the Rule of Many to streamline federal hiring (event known from the title in OPM's news listing; release text not reviewed).
OPM issues guidance telling agencies to stop using the Administrative Careers with America assessment after 36 years, pointing to validated tools such as USA Hire (date from OPM's news listing).

OPM interim final rule removes Uniform Guidelines references from 5 CFR 300.103(c), 330.213, 337.303 and 720.206, citing a 2026-06-09 DOJ OLC opinion; job-analysis and nondiscrimination requirements remain. Comments closed 2026-09-29.

OPM publishes an interim rule on shared certificates and pooled hiring (effective 2026-10-15), aimed at the Merit Hiring Plan goal of drawing at least 60 percent of external competitive selections from shared certificates in FY2027.
OPM time-to-hire memo encourages validated skills-based assessments early in hiring and sets an 80-calendar-day overall standard.

title: Restore skills-based hiring tests and narrow disparate-impact limits on selection
uncertainties: Not verified: whether the Luevano-era consent decree was modified or terminated; whether EEOC/DOJ/Labor changed their parts of the Uniform Guidelines (29 CFR 1607 and related); whether USA Hire is now used at the scale the FY2027 target implies. The Merit Hiring Plan also includes four short essay questions for applicants (guidance 2025-06-23, updated 2026-04-30); I did not read their content, and the Mandate does not mention essay questions. The ACWA release page showed no explicit date, so 2026-02-25 comes from OPM's news listing. The Mandate speaks of USAHire as a testing model; OPM's description of USA Hire as validated assessments is taken from its own pages.
